name: Kansai Nerolac Paints Ltd
title: Kansai Nerolac Paints Ltd - 500165 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 paints call: pricing ~5% consolidated with industrial price hikes still under negotiation, deco volumes low single digit by choice; FY27 margin 13-14% guided to be held, capex INR601 crore over ~2 years with ROCE target ~18%.

summary.headline: Kansai Nerolac Q1 FY27 standalone revenue grew 10.2% with PBDIT up 7.7%; management targets 13-14% margins for FY27 despite input cost pressure.
summary.overview: Standalone net revenue grew 10.2% YoY, PBDIT 7.7% and PBT 5.1%; consolidated revenue rose 9.8%, PBDIT 8.3% and PBT 5.8%. Decorative value growth was high single digit with volume growth low single digit, as the company deliberately shed low-margin volume. Industrial coatings grew double digit in value, but price increases lagged, with about 5% realised so far at customer level. Management announced a INR601 crore capacity expansion across automotive, powder coating and resin, spread over about 2 to 2.5 years, and kept its margin ambition intact.

financial_highlights.metric: Industrial price hike achieved so far
financial_highlights.change: Still under negotiation; effective ask from 1 April

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Value growth high single digit; volume growth low single digit as premium mix was prioritised over low-margin, high-volume products. Economy grew mid-single digit and super premium grew double digit. Margins were stable YoY despite higher ad spend.

segments.name: Industrial (Automotive, Performance Coatings, Powder)
segments.commentary: Value growth double digit. Automotive and powder coating saw strong growth; liquid performance coatings led by construction equipment, drums and coil coating. Gross contribution fell about 1.3% as price increases lagged cost inflation.

segments.name: Auto Refinish
segments.commentary: Growth was flat. Management cited notable premium PU body shop wins and a transition from solvent-borne to waterborne systems that is on plan.

segments.name: Construction chemicals and premium wood finish
segments.commentary: Construction chemicals grew double digit; premium wood finish grew high single digit.

guidance_outlook: FY27 margin ambition of 13-14% is retained, subject to the geopolitical situation not worsening.
Q2 decorative price increase of about 3% expected to flow through; industrial price increase of another 3-5% expected in Q2.

Q2 will carry high-cost inventory and a seasonally weaker quarter, but management expects to maintain margins versus last year's same quarter, helped by sourcing, value engineering and formula optimisation.
Medium term, aim to reach the higher end of the 14%+ margin range within 2-3 years through premiumisation, industrial growth and fixed-cost leverage.
Expected ROCE on incremental capex is towards 18%, with per-KL capex on new capacity lower than the current programme.
Management expects a slightly better festive season, with Diwali in November giving October more painting days in Q3.
capex_capacity: INR601 crore capex for automotive, powder coating and resin capacity at Sayakha, Bawal and Hosur.
Capacity addition of 66,000 KL per year plus resin capacity of close to 10,000 metric tons per year.
The INR601 crore outlay is spread over about 2 to 2.5 years; normal annual capex is INR150-200 crore.
Part of the spend is front-loaded infrastructure, so future incremental capacity will be cheaper per KL.
Industrial capacity is expected to be full in about 2 years, requiring the addition.
demand_pricing: Competitive intensity in decorative remains high, with new entrants still testing the market; no change in pricing discipline, dealer incentives or scheme intensity versus last year or Q4 exit.
Network expansion: 1,700 dealers added in Q1; network additions targeted at 5-10% a year.
Industrial price hike to date about 5%, with more discussions expected to add in Q2.
Solvent inflation was sharp, but solvent inventory is only about 15 days, which made it hard to hedge.
Some free-product schemes continue in certain markets, not specific to the company's focus towns.
Input cost inflation peaked in June and has since eased slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Is decorative volume growth in line with the market, and is competition easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is not below competitors, but the company is deliberately avoiding low-margin, high-volume products. Competitive intensity remains high and is expected to persist through this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins flat YoY when the market leader expanded margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial price increases lag by 1-2 quarters, so the price-cost gap hit industrial gross contribution by about 1.3%. Ad spend rose in Q1 but was offset by mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value growth split in decorative and industrial?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative value growth is high single digit and industrial is double digit. Q1 mix is heavier on decorative, and the mix changes each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the capex and what returns are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: INR601 crore over about 2-2.5 years on top of normal capex of INR150-200 crore per year. Management expects ROCE towards 18%, with lower per-KL capex on new capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pricing growth in Q1 and Q2 on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated pricing was about 4-5% in Q1. Q2 adds about 3% in decorative and another 3-5% in industrial.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any backward integration plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new resin capacity is backward integration for automotive paint, but raw material integration is not on the card. The Kansai Group's global network can supply intermediates as needed.

risks_watch: Geopolitical escalation (West Asia crisis) could raise crude-linked raw material costs and disrupt supply chains.
Rupee depreciation may lift import costs; industrial price negotiations may still be incomplete in Q2.
Decorative volume growth is low single digit, and the company is ceding share in low-margin segments.
Ad and dealer investment is rising, and margin benefit depends on whether premium mix gains come through.
Whether the INR601 crore capacity delivers the targeted ~18% ROCE.
Auto Refinish growth was flat, and the solvent-to-waterborne transition is still in progress.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term plan and on margin resilience, but cautious on near-term industrial pricing and the geopolitical outlook. Management was candid that decorative volume is lagging by design and that competition is not easing.
key_quotes: And that is why I guess for this year, at least that intensity will remain and people will test water in terms of this new set equilibrium.
With that, I'm very confident that this year also, our endeavour is to maintain 13% to 14%.
And on the midterm, I think our endeavour is obviously go to higher end of 14% plus kind of a thing.
